🐾 80K for Autism Assistance Dogs Ireland 🐾
This October, I’m taking on the 80K October Challenge to raise funds for Autism Assistance Dogs Ireland, and I’d really love your support. 💛

If you work with children, you know that every single child we work with is different and that the right support can make such a huge positive difference. For some autistic children and their families, an assistance dog can become a really important part of that support. @autismdogsirl trains assistance dogs to work with autistic children, supporting them and their families in ways that can make a real impact on everyday life.

This feels even more personal for me at the moment because we have been fostering Bramble, a puppy in training with @autismdogsirl , for almost a year now. 🐾 We get to see every day just how much goes into preparing these puppies for the important job they eventually have after graduation. From the tiniest training moments to the bigger milestones, watching Bramble learn and grow has made the work behind an assistance dog feel very real to us!

It costs approximately €25,000 to train one assistance dog, so fundraising is such an important part of making this possible!

Bramble and I will be walking/jogging/running 80K this October, but more importantly, we are hoping to raise as much as possible for AADI along the way so more puppies can become Autism Assistance Dogs too. 💛

If you’d like to support us, you can donate through the link in my bio (there’s also some photos of Bramble in action in the photo album I’ve uploaded when you scroll down on the fundraising page). And if donating isn’t possible, sharing the fundraiser would be hugely appreciated too.

Whether you’re a teacher, SNA, principal, parent or just someone who wants to support this amazing cause, “thank you” from Ciara and Bramble. 🐾💕

Last year in SET I used a scrapbook system for each child on School Support or School Support Plus and a split pin folder/file as a Language Book with my EAL students. This year I’m thinking of using the split pin files/folders with all of my students and call them our Learning Logs. Each child will be designing their own front cover so they have some added ownership over their Learning Log and the collection of work samples we’ll be putting inside during the year ahead. They are very simple but the children seem happy out at the moment picking which clipart they’d like to add (via Canva on my school laptop) and then we print and colour them. There is also the option for a child to choose to just print the blank version and draw their own designs by hand or add some doodles as their cover page.
